events.objective: Establish the true scope and onset of the 401/error spike WITHOUT relying on auth-service logs (log pipeline for identity namespace is down). Using metrics: (1) find the earliest timestamp where auth-service error rate deviates from baseline and whether the onset is a step change or a gradual ramp; (2) determine exactly which fraction of traffic fails and whether failures are uniform across all caller services or concentrated in a subset; (3) check metrics for downstream/upstream neighbors that call auth-service (e.g. gateway, token caches, session stores, user-service) for correlated latency, saturation, CPU/memory/connection-pool exhaustion, or DNS/network anomalies in the same window; (4) determine whether the ~1/3 failure rate is consistent with a partial-fleet or partial-key problem vs a global fault. Report concrete numbers and timestamps.

Find what changed near the onset, across ALL services (not just auth-service). Use get_deployments and get_config_changes over roughly 2026-04-14T00:00Z to 2026-04-15T15:59Z: list every deployment, rollback, feature-flag flip, secret/certificate rotation, and config change touching auth-service AND any shared dependency (token signing keys / JWKS publishing, identity providers, API gateway routing, session stores, IAM/SSO config). Also use get_service_dependencies to build the dependency graph around auth-service and identify shared components whose failure could produce ~36% 401s. Flag any change that plausibly writes/validates tokens or rotates signing material. Correlate timing with the reported symptom window (symptoms first noticed ~14:12Z, data through 15:59Z).

Look for precedent and known failure modes: use search_historical_incidents for prior incidents matching '401', 'invalid_token', 'token validation failure', 'key rotation', 'JWKS/cert expiry', 'identity log pipeline outage', or partial-fleet auth failures. Additionally investigate whether the auth-service log-pipeline outage (identity namespace, down since this morning) could itself be masking or causing the symptom — e.g. same underlying change (config/credential/network) breaking both log shipping and token signing — and whether prior incidents show a recurring coupling between logging outages and auth failures. Report which historical incidents are genuine precedents and what the resolution was.

events.statement: auth-service deployed v7.3.0 at 2026-04-15T14:00:00Z by d.verma, 'Upgrade JWT library to 4.x; refactor token validation', with changes 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)' and 'TokenValidator rewritten'; status live, rolled_back_at null. This is 12 minutes before the 14:12Z report.

A scheduled signing-key rotation config change cfg-2705 on auth-service changed key 'jwt.signing.key_id' from 'k-2025-10' to 'k-2026-04' at 2026-04-15T14:01:00Z by security-automation, one minute after the JWT library deploy and ~11 min before onset.

Two changes in the 14:00–14:01Z window both touch token validation / signing material (JWT parser rewrite and signing key_id rotation); these are the only deployments and only config change in scope (deployments count=2, config changes count=1) for 2026-04-14T00:00Z–2026-04-15T15:59Z across all services.

No rollback occurred for either change: dep-5710 shows rolled_back_at null and status live; the signing-key config change has no rollback/revert entry. Neither change was reverted as of the latest data.

auth-service dependency graph: it calls user-db (postgres), redis-cache (cache), kyc-provider (external), and is called by api-gateway (http). redis-cache is the only component marked shared:true ('shared datastores are used by several services'); all other nodes are shared:false. redis-cache had 0 config changes in the window.

Two precedents match the exact symptom set ('401 invalid_token' / 'users logged out'): HIST-108 (2025-10-01) '401s after JWT signing key rotation' root cause 'Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS' (match_score 6) and HIST-109 (2025-07-11) 'Token validation regression after auth library upgrade' root cause 'JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default' (match_score 5). These are leads, not evidence about the current incident.

The 6-minute-bucket view places the onset in the 14:00:00Z bucket (avg 24.84%, max 38.34%) vs 13:54:00Z (avg 0.25%), which the 2-minute zoom resolves to 14:00→14:02; the plateau level is ~36% (mean ~36.2% per 6-min bucket) at least through 15:54.

events.statement: HIST-108 (2025-10-01) is the closest genuine precedent: '401s after JWT signing key rotation', service auth-service, symptoms '401 invalid_token','users logged out', root cause 'Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS', category config_change, resolution 'Re-published previous key; staged rotation'. Its symptoms and category match the current incident's dominant signals (401 invalid_token, logged-out users) and the cfg-2705 signing-key rotation.

HIST-109 (2025-07-11) is a second genuine precedent with the same symptom signature: 'Token validation regression after auth library upgrade', service auth-service, symptoms '401 invalid_token','token validation failures', root cause 'JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default', category bad_deployment, resolution 'Rolled back; pinned skew config'. This parallels dep-5710's 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)' + 'TokenValidator rewritten'.

Both auth precedents were resolved by reverting the triggering change (HIST-108: 'Re-published previous key'; HIST-109: 'Rolled back'), whereas in the current incident neither candidate change was reverted (dep-5710 status live, rolled_back_at null; cfg-2705 no revert). HIST-101 (auth-service release v6.4.0, 'bcrypt cost factor raised 10->14') is a lower-relevance auth precedent resolved by 'Rolled back v6.4.0' and had different symptoms (latency/CPU/503, not 401s).

No historical precedent was found coupling a logging/observability pipeline outage to auth or token-validation failures. Searches for log-pipeline/identity-namespace outages returned no incident about logs shipping going down; HIST-107 ('Cold cache storm after redis failover', redis-cache) is the only shared-component infra precedent and concerns cache, not logging. The searched corpus contains no incident whose title/root cause links a log pipeline to 401s.

The auth-service dependency graph contains no logging/observability node: nodes are api-gateway (edge, caller), user-db (postgres), redis-cache (redis, shared:true), kyc-provider (external, no telemetry). redis-cache is the only shared component; there is no telemetry-carrying logging component in the graph to correlate with the identity log-pipeline outage. The known-services list also contains no logging/observability service (list spans api-gateway, auth-service, order/portfolio/pricing/market-data/payment/settlement/notification/exchange-gateway, ledger-db, user-db, redis-cache, kafka, exchange-api, bank-partner-api, kyc-provider, email-provider), so the log pipeline is not queryable as a service.

Investigation of logging-touching changes was blocked: get_config_changes(service='logging') failed with not_found ('unknown service logging'); the enumerable known_services list contains no logging/observability component, and a full-scope deployment query for 2026-04-15 returned only dep-5699 (market-data-service, 11:35Z) and dep-5710 (auth-service, 14:00Z) — no logging component appears. So the specific hypothesis that one change broke both log shipping and token signing could not be tested from config/deploy data.

events.answer: Two genuine precedents match the symptom set and both map to the two candidate changes from T2: HIST-108 ('401s after JWT signing key rotation', root cause 'Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS'; resolved by 'Re-published previous key; staged rotation') aligns with cfg-2705's signing-key_id rotation, and HIST-109 ('Token validation regression after auth library upgrade', root cause 'JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default'; resolved by rollback + pinned config) aligns with dep-5710's jjwt 0.11->0.12 parser rewrite. Both were fixed by reverting the trigger, whereas neither current change has been rolled back. I found NO precedent coupling a logging/observability outage to auth failures, and the auth-service dependency graph plus the known-services list contain no logging component — so the identity log-pipeline outage cannot be investigated or linked to token signing from available telemetry; it most plausibly only masks diagnosis (unsearchable auth logs) rather than causing the 401s.

tasks.objective: Establish the true scope and onset of the 401/error spike WITHOUT relying on auth-service logs (log pipeline for identity namespace is down). Using metrics: (1) find the earliest timestamp where auth-service error rate deviates from baseline and whether the onset is a step change or a gradual ramp; (2) determine exactly which fraction of traffic fails and whether failures are uniform across all caller services or concentrated in a subset; (3) check metrics for downstream/upstream neighbors that call auth-service (e.g. gateway, token caches, session stores, user-service) for correlated latency, saturation, CPU/memory/connection-pool exhaustion, or DNS/network anomalies in the same window; (4) determine whether the ~1/3 failure rate is consistent with a partial-fleet or partial-key problem vs a global fault. Report concrete numbers and timestamps.
tasks.answer: auth-service error rate sits at ~0.2% through 13:58–14:00 then jumps in a single step to ~36–37% by 14:02 (bucket resolution 2 min), holding flat at that level through 15:59 — a step change, not a ramp. Traffic (~400 req/s), p99 latency (~90 ms), CPU (~38%), memory, and rate-limiting are all flat across the transition, so ~36% of requests failing points to a partial (≈1/3) failure domain — consistent with a partial-fleet or partial-key problem — with no local saturation; neighbor correlation could not be checked because the tool budget ran out.

tasks.answer: In the window 2026-04-14T00:00Z–2026-04-15T15:59Z there were exactly 2 deployments and 1 config change across all services. The only auth-service-touching changes both land 11–12 minutes before the 14:12Z report: deployment dep-5710 (auth-service v7.3.0, 14:00:00Z, 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)', 'TokenValidator rewritten', live, not rolled back) and config change cfg-2705 (jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 → k-2026-04, scheduled signing-key rotation, 14:01:00Z, security-automation). Both plausibly write/validate tokens or rotate signing material; neither was reverted. The dependency graph shows auth-service sits behind api-gateway and on top of user-db, redis-cache (shared, used by several services), and kyc-provider; the only shared component is redis-cache, which saw 0 config changes. Past incidents HIST-108 (key rotation / JWKS propagation) and HIST-109 (JWT library upgrade skew) are close symptom precedents but are leads only. Data does not by itself establish which of the two changes caused the 401s.

tasks.answer: Two genuine precedents match the symptom set and both map to the two candidate changes from T2: HIST-108 ('401s after JWT signing key rotation', root cause 'Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS'; resolved by 'Re-published previous key; staged rotation') aligns with cfg-2705's signing-key_id rotation, and HIST-109 ('Token validation regression after auth library upgrade', root cause 'JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default'; resolved by rollback + pinned config) aligns with dep-5710's jjwt 0.11->0.12 parser rewrite. Both were fixed by reverting the trigger, whereas neither current change has been rolled back. I found NO precedent coupling a logging/observability outage to auth failures, and the auth-service dependency graph plus the known-services list contain no logging component — so the identity log-pipeline outage cannot be investigated or linked to token signing from available telemetry; it most plausibly only masks diagnosis (unsearchable auth logs) rather than causing the 401s.
